title: Cedaron Wellcare - prospect journal & outreach scaffold
content:
Quick context: Cedaron Wellcare is a mid-size regional managed care org (NY/NJ focus) doing value-based contracts. Heard about them via conference panel (Feb 2025). They have a small ML team (2-3 ICs) and a product org pushing clinical automation and member engagement. Hypothesis: they care about PHI controls, predictable latency for real-time triage suggestions, and cost control for 1M+ monthly messages.

Primary goals for this outreach:
- Get intro call with head of Digital Ops / VP Product (focus: care navigation + member support)
- Pitch a 6-week pilot: Redwood Private (VPC) with a small rep pool + hosted fallback for burst/latency SLOs
- Surface cost/latency savings vs current API vendor + show evals on safety/regression

Key account notes / signals:
- Funding: Series B-ish, but enterprise procurement cycles (vendor questionnaires) — timeline 2-3 months for pilots
- Tech stack: AWS-heavy, some on-prem services for PHI; uses FHIR-compliant data stores (Postgres + custom adapter)
- Compliance posture: HIPAA BAAs required, SOC2 in progress, KMS via AWS KMS likely
- Decision-makers: Head of Digital Ops (K. Moreno), Clinical Ops Director (S. Adler), CTO (J. Park)

Value props we should lean into:
1) Private deployment: customer-managed VPC + KMS/HSM integration (addresses BAAs/PHI)
2) Predictable latency and fallbacks: Dedicated capacity + smart routing to avoid outages during peak queues
3) Cost/perf tooling: batching/cache profiles and Optimize suggestions to cut per-token spend for templated messages
4) Eval tooling: prompt set replays + quality monitoring to detect regressions before/after rollouts

Outbound sequence (concise):
- Email 1 (intro + micro-case): 1-line hook, 2-sentence value (PHI-safe pilot + 30% token savings hypothesis), 1 CTA (15-min intro)
- Email 2 (data + quick ask): short benchmark snapshot (median latency, cost per 1k tokens), ask for tech touch to share logs/traffic shape
- LinkedIn note: reference panel + 1-sentence value: "private inference + predictable SLAs for care workflows"
- Call prep: 20-min agenda, bring a short architecture sketch for private+hosted fallback

Draft Email 1 (subject options):
- "Pilot: Private LLM inference for Cedaron member triage"
- "Reduce inference cost and keep PHI in your VPC — 6-week pilot"

Draft body: 
Hi K.,

I enjoyed your comments on the CareTech panel last week — especially the bit about scaling triage without losing clinical oversight. We help healthcare teams run LLM-based triage and member-engagement flows behind their own VPCs (KMS/HSM support) while keeping predictable latency with dedicated capacity and a hosted fallback for bursts.

Typical pilot: 6 weeks, we run a small dedicated pool, instrument quality checks against your prompt set, and show a cost/latency baseline vs your current vendor. For teams like yours this usually surfaces ~20–40% token-cost savings and fewer timeouts during peak hours.

Would you be open to a quick 15-min intro call next week?

Cheers,
Aisha

Objection handling cheat sheet:
- "We can’t host PHI with a vendor": clarify private deployment option — control plane can be customer-managed, data never leaves VPC; we’ll share BAA template and KMS integration docs.
- "We already have a vendor": ask what they’re missing (latency spikes, blackouts, cost overruns, rollout pain). Offer a non-invasive A/B routing test or dead-man fallback to reduce outages.
- "Procurement slows everything": propose a two-track pilot where engineering runs a self-hosted PoC (on-prem or VPC) while legal spins up procurement — reduces perceived vendor risk.

Technical asks for discovery call:
- Monthly request volume (avg tokens / peak qps)
- Typical sequence lengths and % of long-context requests (>2k tokens)
- Current vendor + known pain points (timeouts, throttling, cost)
- Security/compliance checklist questions they need answered for BAAs

Success metrics for the pilot:
- 99th pct latency under X ms for triage flows (agree target in discovery)
- >15% token cost reduction or equivalent unit economics improvement
- Zero PHI exfiltration incidents; pass BAA/security checklist by week 4

Next actions (my todo):
- Prep a 1-slide architecture sketch for private+fallback (due: Wed 2025-02-19)
- Short benchmark table: Redwood dedicated vs typical vendor (latency/cost) using public models (due: Thu 2025-02-20)
- Slack K. Moreno via mutual connection (Marco Liu) and send intro note (due: Mon 2025-02-17)

Notes to self: keep the first outreach focused on risk-reduction (privacy + reliability) not model bells/whistles. If I get a tech intro, bring up our Optimize tooling to show concrete batching and cache wins for templated triage messages.

Open questions:
- Do they have strict on-call for inference outages? If yes, highlight our graceful degradation policies.
- Are they using embeddings for retrieval today? Could be quick win to show lower-cost rerank pipeline on existing vectors.

Scratch ideas for a cadenced content piece: "How regional payers can run LLMs behind their VPCs — reducing cost, improving uptime" — short one-pager + architecture diagram to share after first call.

End of note.
